solutionSql:
SELECT route_id, id, delivery_due
FROM (
  SELECT s.route_id,
         s.id,
         s.delivery_due,
         ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY s.route_id ORDER BY s.delivery_due, s.id) AS rn
  FROM shipments s
) ranked
WHERE rn <= 2
ORDER BY route_id, delivery_due, id;

rules.howSolved: ROW_NUMBER ordered by delivery_due ascending within each route keeps numbers 1 and 2.
ROW_NUMBER numbers rows distinctly, so a route with at least two shipments returns exactly two rows.
The window ORDER BY adds id ascending after delivery_due, so equal due dates put the lower id first.

ambiguities: A route with exactly one shipment returns that one row. The instruction implies this but does not say it directly.
notes: Sample returns 12 rows, nulls 12, ties 12. A correlated COUNT formulation gives 0 differences on all three datasets.
